title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues an expository letter, which starts on the previous page with the salutation 'Cher Schmik[?]'. That salutation is probably 'Cher Shurik', i.e. addressed to Grothendieck; the neat hand and the remark about motives suggest the writer is Deligne, though this is unconfirmed. The letter supplies the class field theory and complex multiplication background Grothendieck needed for his 'Teichmülleries': Galois actions on objects defined over \bar Q.

(1) Global class field theory for a number field K: Gal(\bar K/K)^{ab} ≅ π_0(A^*/K^*). This is the profinite completion, modulo the connected component, of the idele class group. It is the projective limit of the finite quotients U\A^*/K^*, with U running over open finite-index subgroups of ∏_{v|∞}K_v^* × ∏_{v∤∞}O_v^*.

(2) For U = ∏_{real}R_{>0} × ∏_{complex}C^* × ∏_{v∉S}O_v^* × ∏_{v∈S}(1+m_v^{f_v}), the quotient is the narrow (strict) ray class group of modulus ∏ m_v^{f_v}. Concretely: fractional ideals prime to S, modulo principal ideals (α) with α totally positive and α ≡ 1 mod m_v^{f_v} for v ∈ S.

(3) Chevalley's congruence-subgroup theorem for S-units: every finite-index subgroup of H^0(Spec O − S, O^*) contains a congruence subgroup {x ≡ 1 mod b}. This is what makes the idelic and ideal-theoretic descriptions match.

(4) Local-global compatibility: the local reciprocity map K_v^* → Gal(\bar K_v/K_v)^{ab}, followed by the map to the decomposition group, agrees with the global map composed with K_v^* → A^*/K^*.

(5) Start of the statement of the Shimura–Taniyama main theorem of CM, 'in the form I prefer (except one does not speak enough of motives)'. K is a CM field over a totally real F, with g = [F:Q]. The next page sets up CM abelian varieties up to isogeny with level structure, the reflex field K' as the field of definition of det Lie, and the reflex norm K'^* → K^*.
errors: Minor notational issue: (1+m_v^{f_v})^* has a superfluous '*'.
'S-entier' for α is loose phrasing: α should be a unit at the places of S (implied by the congruence α ≡ 1), not merely S-integral.

missed.claim: Historical: this appears to be an expository letter, probably from Deligne to Grothendieck ('Cher Shurik'), supplying the class field theory and CM background for the Teichmüller/Galois-action project. It documents what arithmetic input Grothendieck was getting around 1981–82.
missed.quote: Voici la façon de l'énoncer que je préfère (sauf qu'on ne parle pas assez de motifs).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest for the history of the Esquisse/anabelian period and the Deligne–Grothendieck exchange. No new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook class field theory and the opening of the standard CM main theorem. The only interest is biographical: an apparent letter to Grothendieck feeding his Galois-Teichmüller work.
transcription_corrections: Previous page salutation 'Cher Schmik[?]' is probably 'Cher Shurik' (Grothendieck's nickname).
'(1+m_v^{f_v})^*' — the trailing * is in the manuscript but is notationally superfluous.
Struck-out word before 'contient' is 'pourtant' (deleted); correctly marked.
